messages:
Elena Park: Heads-up — during our onboarding demo I hit two problems with the Next starter (App Router + LangChain agent + LlamaIndex): 1) duplicate inference calls during SSR on edge providers, and 2) flaky eval harness failures because of streaming framing differences between JS/Python.
Elena Park: Repro for duplicate calls: deploy starter to Vercel Edge, load /agent-ssr with a single question -> telemetry shows two upstream requests, token counts doubled.
Elena Park: Server handler (trimmed):
```js
export const runtime = 'edge';
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js';
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
export async function POST(req) {
  const { q } = await req.json();
  const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rw-llama-7b', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: q }] });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(resp));
}
```
Elena Park: Logs show transport retry + sdk retry sequence:
[2026-06-12T10:14:01Z] transport: fetch failed status=429 retrying
[2026-06-12T10:14:01Z] sdk: retry attempt=2 idempotency=null
Elena Park: For the streaming flake, our eval harness in starter-templates expects a final framed chunk {"final":true,"text":"..."} but the JS SDK historically closes streams without emitting that final framed JSON chunk; Python emits it. CI intermittently times out joining deltas.
Gabe Turner: Two separable but related issues: (A) missing idempotency headers in server contexts leads to double-exec when transport and sdk both retry; (B) streaming event parity between JS/Python causes eval flakes. Good catch.
Marta Ruiz: Short-term mitigations we used in the demo: 1) set explicit header 'Idempotency-Key: <uuid>' in the starter server handler, 2) in the harness accept stream close as final and join deltas. Both stop customer-facing flakes immediately.
Gabe Turner: For the duplication bug I'd prefer an SDK-side fix: auto-add an Idempotency-Key for server/edge runtimes and also pin per-request auth credentials so a retry doesn't accidentally switch to a rotated key. Python already does this; JS should mirror.
Marta Ruiz: Agreed. I experimented with a small wrapper that snapshots the API key at request start and injects an Idempotency-Key; that removed duplicates even when rotate-in-background code was present.
Elena Park: We also saw a case where a background key refresher swapped the cached key mid-request; later retry used new key and the backend considered it a distinct invocation. The logs looked like:
[2026-06-12T10:14:01Z] auth: rotating key -> key_b
[2026-06-12T10:14:02Z] transport: retry attempt=2 Authorization=Bearer key_b
Elena Park: So per-request credential pinning is a must for serverless starters that do rotation.
Gabe Turner: Action items I can take: open an SDK PR to implement 1) per-request credential pinning, 2) auto-idempotency in server/edge contexts (opt-out flag), and 3) a stream framing parity mode where JS emits a final chunk object by default. I'll add unit tests that simulate transport retries and mid-request rotation.
Marta Ruiz: I can draft starter-templates PR that: detects server runtime (typeof window === 'undefined' || runtime === 'edge'), passes client config { autoIdempotency: true }, and updates README with a note about server runtimes, ephemeral keys, and the recommended createServerClient helper. Also update the eval harness to canonicalize streams (accept final chunk OR stream-close) while waiting for SDK fix.
infra-bot: Created ticket: starter-templates#512 "agent-starter: server idempotency + stream parity" and linked platform-sdk#2301
Gabe Turner: I'll target SDK release v0.10.0 for these changes and include a compatibility flag for consumers that relied on the old streaming behavior. Will also add an acceptance test that runs both JS and Python against the mock streaming server and asserts identical framed sequences.
Elena Park: One more small DX note: onboarding ZIP we hand to users should be updated (quickstart.zip) so new users don't get bitten by examples that lack these protections. Please coordinate with docs to update the quickstart and the "Server runtimes and idempotency" short guide.
Marta Ruiz: I'll raise a follow-up PR to update quickstart.zip once the SDK PR merges. Meanwhile I'll cherry-pick the explicit Idempotency-Key example into the starter README so demos are safe.
devex-bot: Issue platform-sdk#2301 created and assigned to @Gabe Turner with milestone v0.10.0
Gabe Turner: Thanks for the repro and logs, Elena — will ping here when the draft PR is up. :thumbsup:
Elena Park: Thanks all. Happy to run more stress tests on Vercel/Netlify after patches land.
